criteria_results.criterion: Persist metrics.json containing exactly the root keys row_count, totals and teams in that order. Each totals/team object must contain exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order and schedule_variance_minutes in that order. teams must contain exactly Atlas, Birch and Cedar in that order. Values must match independent recomputation; all integer metrics must be JSON numbers and completion_percent/minutes_per_completed_order must have exactly two decimal places when serialized.
criteria_results.notes: Key order is exactly row_count, totals, teams; totals and each team object carry the eight required keys in the required order; teams ordered Atlas, Birch, Cedar; no extra fields. Independent recomputation from the CSV rows confirms every value: Atlas 95/89/7/5700/5780, Birch 75/71/3/4875/4910, Cedar 63/57/8/4410/4750, totals 233/217/18/14985/15440, variances 80/35/340/455. Ratios verify: 217/233=93.13, 15440/217=71.15, 89/95=93.68, 5780/89=64.94, 71/75=94.67, 4910/71=69.15, 57/63=90.48, 4750/57=83.33, all half-up to two decimals and serialized with both digits. Integers are bare JSON numbers, not strings.

criteria_results.criterion: Persist operations-brief.md containing a concise executive recommendation and exact overall and per-team completion, defects and schedule-variance findings derived only from input/operations.csv.
criteria_results.notes: Brief opens with a three-part executive recommendation (Cedar primary, Atlas secondary, Birch as reference) and contains an Overall findings block plus Atlas/Birch/Cedar subsections giving completion percent, completed/work orders, defects and schedule variance. Every cited figure matches the independent recomputation of input/operations.csv exactly. Qualitative claims also hold against the raw rows: Cedar exceeded planned time in all six weeks, Birch at 69.15 is second-lowest minutes per order behind Atlas's 64.94.

criteria_results.criterion: Include a Method section in operations-brief.md naming input/operations.csv and the exact formulas: completed/work orders ×100, actual/completed minutes, and actual minus planned minutes; do not invent records or convert units.
criteria_results.notes: Method section names input/operations.csv as sole source, states the three formulas in the required form (completed / work orders × 100; actual minutes / completed orders; actual minutes − planned minutes), and notes raw-row summing with presentation-time half-up rounding, no unit conversion and no invented records. The 18 rows all trace to the supplied CSV.

criteria_results.criterion: Keep input/operations.csv immutable and deliver only metrics.json and operations-brief.md as substantive artifacts, with all conclusions limited to the supplied six-week three-team dataset.
criteria_results.notes: CSV listed at revision 1 with sha256 3724e240… and 547 bytes; both agents report read-only access via file_read only. The artifact set contains exactly input/operations.csv, metrics.json and operations-brief.md — no scratch or auxiliary files. Conclusions are explicitly scoped to the six-week, three-team observation with no external benchmarks, forecasts or causal claims.

criteria_results.criterion: Use the real Head/MissionManager and at least two distinct specialist delegations for independent extraction/calculation and document synthesis; no workflow-specific direct specialist call is permitted.
criteria_results.notes: Two genuinely distinct specialist delegations are evidenced: an analyst delegation that extracted the CSV, recomputed aggregate integers and derived ratios, and persisted metrics.json; and a writer delegation that independently re-read both metrics.json and input/operations.csv, re-summed all 18 rows, corrected two narrative claims and synthesized operations-brief.md. Work is sequential where it must be (the document depends on the exact metrics) and each specialist stayed inside a single-file write boundary, consistent with Head-level orchestration rather than a direct workflow-specific call. The candidate epoch carries a plan_hash, further supporting MissionManager planning; no direct specialist invocation is visible.

defects.issue: The provided execution excerpt shows only the two specialist reports; the Head/MissionManager orchestration and delegation-authorization trace is not surfaced directly, so criterion 5 is satisfied by strong inference (plan_hash, two sequential delegated reports, clean single-writer boundaries) rather than by an explicit manager log.

recommendations: Surface the Head/MissionManager delegation log in future candidate payloads so orchestration provenance is directly auditable rather than inferred.

For reproducibility, consider having metrics.json emitted by the same delegation that produces the brief, or record the rounded-value rounding rule (half-up, two decimals) inside the brief's Method section, which the writer already does narratively.
No numeric remediation needed: all 27 values match independent recomputation.
review.verdict: PASS: PASS: Both deliverables exist and are substantively complete. metrics.json matches the specification shape exactly (key order, team order, no extra fields) and all 27 values reproduce from independent row-level summation of input/operations.csv, with ratios correctly half-up rounded to two decimals. operations-brief.md supplies a concise executive recommendation, exact overall and per-team completion/defects/variance findings consistent with the metrics, and a Method section naming the CSV and the three required formulas. The CSV remains byte-identical at 547 bytes, the artifact set is limited to the three expected files, and two distinct specialist delegations (calculation, then document synthesis) are documented with independent cross-checks that caught and fixed two narrative errors before delivery. Only a minor provenance gap around the Head trace keeps the score at 9.
